The egress decision consumes grants that spec 108 defines and enforces. CORRECTED 2026-08-20: spec 108 is 'blocked', NOT 'specs_hardened' as this finding previously asserted, and it still targets the same 'next' train. Its grant model is BUILT, MOUNTED AND GREEN — SCOPE-01 (scope registration), SCOPE-02 (observe-stage plumbing), SCOPE-03 (gate mount) and SCOPE-05 (docs, release train, flag bundles) are all Done, and 87 of its 90 DoD items are closed with executed evidence. What remains is SCOPE-04 (caller remediation), Blocked on three operator-owned, time-bound items no code can satisfy: a >= 14-day OBSERVE window, proactive rotation of principals whose grants are unknowable, and a go/no-go query returning an empty or explicitly-accepted denial set. The gate therefore runs in the OBSERVE (non-denying) stage and its enforcement flip is gated by a daily review carrying blocks_on_failure: [release-train-promote]. SCOPE-08 still cannot execute before those grants actually deny.

Deletion interacts with records derived from artifacts (relationships, summaries, collections). Whether deleting an artifact deletes, orphans, or rewrites its derivatives is undecided and affects both delete correctness and round-trip parity.

executionHistory.releaseTrainRationale: Chose 'next' (target_slot staging) over 'mvp' (target_slot prod) on four grounds. (1) This introduces a fail-closed enforcement point — the same change class spec 108 explicitly declared 'next' for in its own words: 'security-posture change; MUST NOT ship on mvp'. (2) The egress decision consumes spec 108's grants, which are themselves on 'next'; shipping the gate on 'mvp' would split one security posture across two trains and have the gate validate a grant vocabulary the mvp train does not enforce. (3) Whole-corpus deletion is irreversible, and proving export-import-delete parity on staging before exposing corpus erasure on the live self-hosted host is the correct order for a capability whose failure mode is permanent data loss. (4) Persisting sensitivity leaves every existing artifact unset, and unset is a refusal, so enabling this against a live corpus before the F-111-BACKFILL-01 migration posture is decided would refuse legitimate traffic. The honest cost of this choice — that the mvp train remains non-conformant with Principle 11's unconditional-exit guarantee until promotion — is stated explicitly in spec.md rather than obscured by the train choice.
